answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make trust costly to fake by tying reputation to locked collateral instead of free identities. Each agent first bonds stake into a shared harbor, and an ocean-wide beacon quorum cross-checks every attestation against ledger history. A newcomer plants a juniper-sized bond per identity, so mass sybils scale attacker cost linearly while honest agents only risk their own stake — the attack economics collapse before vote weight ever matters.
